newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: S.Korean union offers end strike if law put off - TV.
newsitem.headline: S.Korean union offers end strike if law put off - TV.

text.p: South Korea's strike leaders have offered to end stoppages if the government agrees to delay implementation of a controversial labour law, state television reported on Saturday.
It said the offer was conveyed by South Korea's Roman Catholic cardinal Stephen Kim when he met President Kim Young-sam on Friday.
A spokesman of the outlawed Korean Confederation of Trade Unions, which has been spearheading more than three weeks of strikes, declined to confirm the report.
"Our position will be announced in a news conference later today," he said.

The cardinal told reporters after he met the president that he appealed to the government to end the current crisis caused by the labour law through dialogue, but he gave no other details of their meeting at the presidential Blue House.
The confederation has so far ruled out any compromise with the government unless it repeals the law, which allows companies to lay off workers, replace strikers and change working hours.
